@homeSettings.description: Tooltip of the gear button on the home screen that opens Settings.

@homeYourDevices.description: Section label above the list of paired devices (shown in capitals).

@homeNearbyNotPaired.description: Section label above devices found on the network but not paired yet (shown in capitals).

@homeAddDevice.description: Floating button on the home screen that starts pairing a new device.

@homeVisible.description: Line under the top bar: this phone can be found by other devices. name is this phone's name.

@homeUpdateTitle.description: Title of a warning card when the computers run a newer protocol than this app.

homeUpdateBody: Your computers now speak a newer Linksy than this app.

@homeUpdateBody.description: Body of the update warning card.

@homeGetUpdate.description: Button on the update warning card that opens the download page.

@homeSendFiles.description: Accessibility label of the round send button on a device row.

@homePair.description: Button on a nearby unpaired device row that starts pairing.

@homeStepChoose.description: Step 2 of 'Connect your first device'. “Pair with QR Code” is the desktop app's menu item; translate it as the desktop app does.

@homeStepScan.description: Step 3 of 'Connect your first device'; 'it' is the QR code.

@homeConnectTitle.description: Large title on the empty home screen. Keep the line break where it reads well.

homeConnectSubtitle: Straight over your Wi-Fi. No account, no cloud.

@homeScanQr.description: Main button on the empty home screen that opens the QR scanner.

@homePairByAddress.description: Secondary button on the empty home screen: pair by typing the computer's IP address.

@pairingAddDevice.description: Title of the 'Add a device' bottom sheet.

pairingAddDeviceHint: On the other device, open Linksy and choose “Pair with QR Code”.

@pairingAddDeviceHint.description: Hint in the 'Add a device' sheet. “Pair with QR Code” is the desktop app's menu item.

@pairingScanQr.description: Option in the 'Add a device' sheet that opens the QR scanner.

@pairingScanQrCaption.description: Caption under 'Scan QR code' in the 'Add a device' sheet.

@pairingByAddress.description: Option in the 'Add a device' sheet, and title of the dialog to type a computer's IP address.

pairingByAddressCaption: When the other device can’t be found.

@pairingByAddressCaption.description: Caption under 'Pair by address' in the 'Add a device' sheet.

@pairingWith.description: Snack bar while pairing starts with a device. name is the device's name.

@pairingWithOtherDevice.description: Snack bar while pairing starts from a pairing link that carries no device name.

pairingAddressHint: It’s in Linksy’s Preferences on the other device.

@pairingAddressHint.description: Hint in the 'Pair by address' dialog: where to find the address.

@pairingPortHint.description: Hint under the address field: the default network port. port is a number like 47200; do not format it.

@pairingPair.description: Button in the 'Pair by address' dialog that starts pairing.

@pairingWantsToPair.description: Title of the pairing dialog when another device asked to pair. name is that device's name.

@pairingPairWith.description: Title of the pairing dialog when this phone asked to pair. name is the other device's name.

pairingCodeHint: Both screens should show this code.

@pairingCodeHint.description: Under the pairing dialog title, above the 6-digit code.

@pairingCodeLabel.description: Accessibility label of the 6-digit pairing code. code is like '123 456'.

@pairingCodesMatch.description: Button in the pairing dialog to accept: the codes on both screens are the same.

scanNeedsCamera: Linksy needs the camera to scan the pairing code. Allow it, or pair by address.

@scanNeedsCamera.description: Shown in the scanner when camera permission was refused.

@scanCameraUnavailable.description: Shown in the scanner when the camera can't start.

@scanFlashlight.description: Tooltip of the flashlight button in the QR scanner.

@scanTitle.description: Large title over the QR scanner's camera view.

scanWrongCode: That’s not a Linksy code. On your computer, open Linksy → Pair with QR Code.

@scanWrongCode.description: Shown in the scanner when a QR code that isn't a Linksy pairing code was scanned. 'Pair with QR Code' is the desktop app's menu item.

scanHint: On your computer, open Linksy and choose “Pair with QR Code”.

@scanHint.description: Hint at the bottom of the QR scanner. “Pair with QR Code” is the desktop app's menu item.

@shareSheetPutOnClipboard.description: Title of the share sheet when one shared file goes onto a computer's clipboard.

@shareSheetSendFiles.description: Title of the share sheet when files were shared to Linksy from another app.

@shareSheetOpenOnComputer.description: Title of the share sheet when a web link was shared: it opens in a computer's browser.

@shareSheetSendToClipboard.description: Title of the share sheet when text was shared: it goes to a computer's clipboard.

shareSheetNoClipboardFiles: None of your computers takes files on its clipboard yet. Update Linksy there.

@shareSheetNoClipboardFiles.description: Share sheet, no computer supports files on its clipboard.

shareSheetNoComputers: Pair a computer first, then share to it from any app.

@shareSheetNoComputers.description: Share sheet, no paired computer yet.

@shareSheetSendFileInstead.description: Share sheet button: send the file normally rather than onto the clipboard.

shareSheetClipboardInstead: Put it on the computer’s clipboard instead

@shareSheetClipboardInstead.description: Share sheet button: put the one shared file onto the computer's clipboard.

@shareSheetOpenLinkInstead.description: Share sheet button: open the shared link in the computer's browser.

shareSheetSendAsTextInstead: Send as text to the clipboard instead

@shareSheetSendAsTextInstead.description: Share sheet button: send the shared link as text to the computer's clipboard.

@shareSheetPuttingOnClipboard.description: Snack bar after sharing a file onto a computer's clipboard. name is the computer's name.

shareSheetPuttingOnClipboardUnnamed: Putting it on the computer’s clipboard

@shareSheetPuttingOnClipboardUnnamed.description: Snack bar after sharing a file onto a computer's clipboard, when its name isn't known.

@shareSheetOpened.description: Snack bar after a shared link was opened on a computer. name is the computer's name.

@shareSheetOpenedUnnamed.description: Snack bar after a shared link was opened on a computer whose name isn't known.

@shareSheetSentToClipboard.description: Snack bar after shared text was sent to a computer's clipboard. name is the computer's name.

@shareSheetSentToClipboardUnnamed.description: Snack bar after shared text was sent to a computer's clipboard, when its name isn't known.

@shareSheetSentALink.description: Title of the dialog when a computer sent a web link to this phone. name is the computer's name.

@shareSheetOpen.description: Button in the received-link dialog: open the link on this phone.

@shareSheetCopyLink.description: Button in the received-link dialog: copy the link.

@shareSheetLinkCopied.description: Snack bar after copying a received link.

incomingSendingYou: {name} is sending you {count, plural, =1{a file} other{{count} files}}

@incomingSendingYou.description: Title of the incoming-files sheet. name is the sending device's name (shown in a stronger color).

@incomingTotal.description: Total size of the incoming files. size is like '2.1 MB'.

@incomingMore.description: Under the first few incoming file names: how many more files there are.

@incomingAccept.description: Button in the incoming-files sheet: receive the files.

@appInvalidPairingLink.description: Snack bar when a linksy:// pairing link can't be read.

@appPairingFailed.description: Snack bar when pairing failed. reason is an explanation (may be in English).

@appCouldntPair.description: Snack bar when pairing with a device failed. name is the device's name; reason is an explanation.

@appPairedWith.description: Snack bar when pairing succeeded. name is the device's name.

@appNotification.description: Snack bar showing a notification a computer sent: its name, then the notification's text.

@appCopiedText.description: Snack bar when a computer put text on this phone's clipboard. name is the computer's name.

@appCopiedFile.description: Snack bar when a computer put a file on this phone's clipboard. file is the file name; name is the computer's name.

@appCouldntStart.description: Title of the screen shown when the app fails to start; an error message follows.

@commonDismiss.description: Tooltip of the close button on a notice card.

@commonDecline.description: Button to refuse a pairing request or incoming files.

@commonNotNow.description: Button that closes a dialog without doing anything.

@commonConnected.description: A device's status: connected right now.

@commonNearby.description: A device's status: found on the same network, not connected.

@commonNotNearby.description: A device's status: not found on the network.

@commonUsbCable.description: How a device is reached, in lists: over a USB cable.

@commonAwayFromHome.description: How a device is reached, in lists: over the internet (not on the same Wi-Fi).

@commonSameWifi.description: How a device is reached, in lists: on the same Wi-Fi network.

@commonConnectedByUsb.description: A device's status: connected over a USB cable.

@commonConnectedAway.description: A device's status: connected over the internet.

@commonBattery.description: Accessibility label of a device's battery ring. level is 0 to 100.

@commonBatteryCharging.description: Accessibility label of a device's battery ring while it charges. level is 0 to 100.

@formatBytesSmall.description: A size under 1 kB, like '512 bytes'.

formatSecondsLeft: {count, plural, =1{1 second left} other{{count} seconds left}}
formatMinutesLeft: {count, plural, =1{1 minute left} other{{count} minutes left}}
formatHoursLeft: {count, plural, =1{about 1 hour left} other{about {count} hours left}}

@formatHoursLeft.description: Time left in a transfer, rounded.

@formatToday.description: Day heading in a device's timeline.

@formatYesterday.description: Day heading in a device's timeline.

@formatPhone.description: Name of this phone's main storage in folder paths, like 'Phone › Download › Linksy'.
